reviewer: adversarial finder (score not authoritative; see PROMPT-STANDARD "How to review a prompt")

gaps.problem: Item 21 is unachievable as written and its supporting §6 bullet is technically wrong. The hint must fade 'over ≤ 3 s of dt (not a CSS-only animation, so it is deterministic under speed=0)'. But registry.update(dt) is fed raw wall-derived dt in src/main.js:121-127 regardless of clock speed, so dt keeps flowing at speed=0 — a dt-driven fade is exactly as capture-timing-dependent as a CSS one. screenshot.mjs waits for __sim.ready, then 400–600 ms, then --measure 1.5 s, so a ≤3 s fade is fully expired before the shutter. Item 11 and §8 both require photo_22.png to show 'a fading hint', so the builder is asked for a visible hint that the same item guarantees will be gone. The builder will implement dt, look at the shot, see nothing, and burn a round.
gaps.fix: Replace the mechanism clause: 'the hint's opacity is a pure function of accumulated game time and is pinned at 1.0 whenever world.time.speed === 0'. Then make the item observable: 'in photo_22.png the hint rect is ≥ 120×24 px with computed opacity ≥ 0.5; no other #ui descendant has a non-zero visible rect.' Rewrite the §6 bullet to say the defect is any capture-time-dependent fade (CSS transition or dt alike), not CSS specifically.

gaps.problem: Item 3's six-rail mapping fights §3's own visual target and has undefined probe operands. world.economy.demand.residential is a single 0..1 value; rails 1–3 = residential × 0.40/0.35/0.25 means the three green rails can never exceed 40 %/35 %/25 % fill even at maximum residential demand, while §3 describes cs2_3's green bars as the long ones and tells the builder 'rebuild it in the CS2 form'. A builder who follows the rule gets a widget that reads as permanently low demand and loses on §3 fidelity; one who normalises fails the probe. Separately, the probe 'checks each rail's getBoundingClientRect().width ratio against factor × demand[key] within 3 %' never says ratio of what to what, and no selector is named for the fill element versus the rail, even though item 1 and the selectors-map rule name selectors everywhere else.
gaps.fix: Make the split thresholding rather than scaling: 'rail n shows clamp((residential − t_n) / w_n, 0, 1) with t = [0, 0.33, 0.66], w = 0.34' — three staged green rails that each reach full fill, which is what cs2_3 shows. And name the operands: '.sb-rci-b (rail) and its child .sb-rci-f (fill); the probe compares fill.width / rail.width against the computed fraction within 3 %', adding both to the selectors-map requirement.

gaps.problem: The spec's own pass rubric conflicts with CRITIC.md. The 8.5 anchor is 'Items 1–8 all pass, ≥ 8 of items 9–19 pass, no hard fail' — items 9–19 is eleven items, so a build can fail item 19 (Budget: maxDrawCalls ≤ 20, maxTriangles ≤ 300 000, moduleMs.ui ≤ 1.0 mean) and still be scored 8.5 by this spec. CRITIC.md states 'Pass requires all of: score ≥ 8.5 · zero console errors · module status ready in every shot · draw calls within the declared budget · API contract satisfied', and CS2-LOOK.md lists over-budget draw calls as a hard fail regardless of look. Item 4's header says the critic grades only this list, so the two documents give opposite answers on the same build.
gaps.fix: Move item 19 into the 1–8 block (making it 1–9 with 'all pass'), or add one line under the anchor table: 'Item 19 is a hard fail, not a tie-breaker — an over-budget build caps at 7 regardless of items 1–18, per CRITIC.md.' Same treatment for item 12's zero-console-errors clause.

gaps.problem: The card and category inventory is unbounded, and it is the largest single piece of work in the round. Item 6 requires 'every card in every category' to be a hand-authored 3/4 perspective SVG/canvas with ≥ 4 distinct fills, ≥ 3 tonal steps of one hue, and a contact shadow at 3–15 % of card area. Item 4 requires ≥ 14 category icons but never lists the categories. The only card floors anywhere are 'services ≥ 8 cards' (item 11) and '≥ 6 cards per row at 1080p, wrapping to a second row' (item 6). One builder ships 5 categories × 7 cards = 35 thumbnails; another reads 'every category' against 14 icons and ships 100+. Both are technically compliant, and the 8 vs 9 anchor ('cards or icons still read schematic' vs 'nits only in card art') turns entirely on which one they chose.
gaps.fix: Add to item 6: 'The toolbar declares exactly these N categories: <list>. Total cards across all categories ≥ 48 and ≤ 72; every category has ≥ 4 cards, the roads and services categories ≥ 8. docs/builds/ui_r3.json declares cardCounts: {categoryId: n}.' Pin the category list in §3's toolbar-contents paragraph so item 4's ≥ 14 has named members.

gaps.problem: Item 13's probe does not test what the item claims. It mutates world.economy.money by +50 000 and demand.commercial to 0.9, then forces a tick via simulation.api.step(1) — but runTick() recomputes the economy from the simulation's own model (src/modules/simulation/index.js:187 → runTick), so both injected values are overwritten before the HUD reads them. The item then only asserts 'the money chip and the C bar both change within 1 s of that tick', which any tick produces regardless of whether the mutations were ever visible. The builder will inject +50 000, watch the chip not show it, and spend time debugging a binding that is correct.
gaps.fix: Drop the tick from the binding half: 'mutate world.economy.money by +50 000 and demand.commercial to 0.9, then wait one animation frame; the money chip text and the C rail width reflect the mutated values (no tick — ui reads world every frame).' Keep the forced-tick paragraph as a separate assertion that the chips also move on sim:tick, and keep the step(1)/setSpeed recipe there since that part is accurate and useful.

gaps.problem: §7 restates BUILDER.md content, despite the spec's opening line claiming 'nothing in either is repeated here' and 'nothing from that list is restated here'. The closing paragraph of §7 ('ui must never: add a light, install a composer, call renderer.render, set toneMapping/scene.fog, touch another module's group') is BUILDER.md's 'Stay in your lane' bullet; the ctx.rng function list (float/int/range/pick/weighted/gauss/shuffle/fork) duplicates BUILDER.md's determinism bullet; 'Core changes go in docs/core-requests/ui.md' duplicates BUILDER.md's writable-files list. These are exactly the lines that drift when BUILDER.md changes, and the spec is otherwise scrupulous about delegation.
gaps.fix: Cut the three duplicated fragments. Keep only the ui-specific half of the lane rule — 'ui owns no world section and adds no scene content outside its own showcase backdrop' — and replace the rng list with 'ctx.rng: see BUILDER.md.' The header's no-repetition claim then becomes true.

gaps.problem: §5 and §8 give two incompatible draw-call ceilings. §5: 'Draw calls (ui showcase, incl. environment) ≤ 20'. §8: the backdrop 'All of it inside ctx.group, ≤ 20 draw calls.' Environment contributes ~7 (r1 measured 11 total = environment 7 + backdrop 4; r2 measured 14 total), so the backdrop's real ceiling under §5 is ~13, not 20. Item 19's probe reads maxDrawCalls across the gauntlet, i.e. the total, so §5 is the operative rule and §8 is simply wrong — but a builder budgeting the §8 scene list (merged streets with markings/kerbs/sidewalks, instanced facades, park block, trees, ≥ 40 lamps) against 20 rather than 13 will overshoot and have to re-merge late.
gaps.fix: In §8 change '≤ 20 draw calls' to '≤ 13 draw calls (§5 caps the ui showcase at 20 including environment's ~7)'.

gaps.problem: Two factual errors that a builder acting on them would get wrong. §7 says 'tools, props, services, infoviews and transit are still stubs (api: {} / api:{serialize,deserialize})' — props is not a stub, it has a full api at src/modules/props/index.js:234 (rebuild, stats, lamps, signal state). And §3's night paragraph cites '$REF/cs2_8.jpg for the scene', but the ref directory contains cs2_1.jpg…cs2_7.jpg only; cs2_8.jpg does not exist (CS2-LOOK.md and roads.md/transit.md make the same broken promise, so this is a project-wide stale reference the spec inherited).
gaps.fix: Drop props from the stub list (it is not in ui's optional-module table anyway, so the sentence loses nothing). Change the night citation to 'cs2_3 for the HUD; there is no night HUD reference in $REF, so item 14's measurements are the whole requirement' — the §3 preamble already establishes that numbers outrank images, so this costs nothing.

gaps.problem: Two acceptance items have a checkable-sounding clause with no threshold or no method. Item 4: 'an icon passes if its two largest bins are ≥ 25° apart' is stated but never given a count — if three of fifteen icons fail that per-icon test, does the item fail? The only stated row-level threshold is the separate pairwise-distinctness clause (≥ 8 icons), leaving the per-icon clause orphaned and arguable. Item 8: 'Every numeric value right-aligned within its pill' has no probe, while the structurally identical requirement in item 9 does ('the right edges of all .sb-v in a section agree within 1 px').
gaps.fix: Item 4: append '…and ≥ 12 of the icons individually satisfy the two-largest-bins test.' Item 8: append 'probe: within each pill, the right edge of the numeric span and the pill's content-box right edge agree within 2 px.'

gaps.problem: The §5 budget table carries four rows with no observation method and no acceptance item behind them — 'JS heap attributable to ui ≤ 24 MB' (__sim.stats().heapMB is whole-process, not per-module), 'GPU texture memory (ui showcase) ≤ 24 MB', 'Per-frame allocation in update(): none', and 'DOM ≤ 1800 elements under #ui'. Item 19 grades only drawCalls, triangles and moduleMs, and item 4's header says what is not on the list is not required, so these four are decorative. The DOM one is the only one that is trivially checkable and it is the one most worth enforcing, given item 6 asks for dozens of SVG thumbnails.
gaps.fix: Add to item 19: 'plus document.querySelectorAll("#ui *").length ≤ 1800 in the ui preset with all panels open.' Delete the JS-heap, texture-memory and per-frame-allocation rows from §5, or mark them explicitly 'not graded — engineering guidance only', so they do not read as requirements the critic must invent a method for.

gaps.problem: The panel base colour is never given, though the accent is nailed to rgb(83,177,212) with the crop it came from. §3 supplies alphas (0.36 toolbar, 0.73 status strip, ~85 % info panel) and one descriptive phrase, 'translucent dark navy', but no hex for the fill those alphas apply over, and item 14 only constrains pill fill luminance to a wide 18–90 band. Two builders will land on #0d1117 and #101a2c and the difference is visible beside cs2_5, yet nothing in the acceptance list distinguishes them.
gaps.fix: Add one sentence to §3's info-panel paragraph with the measured value: 'panel fill rgb(R,G,B) sampled from cs2_5 at <crop>, i.e. --panel: #RRGGBB', and add its hue/lightness tolerance to item 5 alongside --accent so one probe covers both tokens.

gaps.property: 2 (Rules for module specs, item 2: copy the signatures)
gaps.problem: §2's world-data section is reformatted into running prose rather than copied as a block from ARCHITECTURE §3, and the reformatting silently truncates real section shapes: world.services is given as {items,kinds,supply,demand} but also carries coverage(), place(), remove() and version; world.infoview is given as {active,data,legend} but also carries buildingTint(id); world.transit as {lines,stops} but also carries version. The field names ui actually reads are all correct, so the damage is small, but it is precisely the paraphrase-and-drift the standard forbids — and the §15-added fields ui depends on (economy.milestone, economy.loans, economy.grids) exist only in simulation's writes, not in src/core/world.js, which the prose does flag but does not source.
gaps.fix: Replace the prose paragraph with a fenced code block copied from ARCHITECTURE §3 for economy/time/weather/selection/flags plus §15's services/infoview/transit shapes, marking the ui-read fields, and cite src/modules/simulation/index.js:204-212 as the source for milestone()/loans()/grids() being present only when simulation is loaded.

strengths: Property 3 is close to exemplary — nearly every visual requirement carries a measured source, a crop rect and a tolerance (band alpha 0.32–0.46 sampled at x 900–1100 y 985–1001, accent hue 190–202° / sat 50–72 % / light 52–64 % from cs2_1 x 782–850 y 868–928, dock 58–64 px + 44–52 px ≤ 115 px). A builder cannot satisfy these two different ways.

Property 4 is handled better than any generic scale: the spec explicitly overrides ARCHITECTURE §13's photorealism anchors (correctly citing CRITIC.md's 'ui is scored as an interface against the CS2 HUD') and supplies a bespoke 10/9/8.5/8/7/5 table where each rung names an observable artefact, including a real r1 shot at the 5 anchor.

Property 10 is real, not boilerplate: every §6 bullet traces to docs/critic/ui_r1.md issues 1–12 or to ui_r2.json's remainingWeaknesses (mid-glyph ellipsis at 10.5 px, lamp halos clipping near-white, photo hint on a CSS fade, transit/info sharing the left slot) — I checked all four against the file. The environment traps (screenshots never hover, static DOM makes 16 identical frames, Vite full-reload boot-splash frames under ~400 KB) are specific to this box and this project.

Dependency accuracy is verified: index.js:19, main.js:82, main.js:91, registry.js:14, world.js:91 are all exactly right, every selector in item 1 exists in src/modules/ui/*.js, the claim that params.camera is applied after showcase.setup is true (main.js:99 vs :105), and the ctx.clock/camera/events/assets/rng/save.js signatures match source including defaults (flyTo seconds=2, sunElevation(hour=this.hour), dayLengthSeconds=600).

Item 15 resolves two ownership questions that r2 had settled unilaterally in a build report (the 1440 px breakpoint, and info > legend > statistics precedence) by promoting them into the spec and requiring them declared in ui_r3.json — exactly the right fix for spec drift, and item 1's 720p clause cross-checks it by asserting the closed panels are .sb-hidden rather than merely off-screen.

Item 14 pre-empts a foreseeable builder/critic argument by name, ruling that CRITIC.md's p99≥250 / p1≤5 blown/crushed limits are a scene rule that must not be applied to white HUD glyphs on near-black pills. That is one saved round.
verdict: 8.0 — FAIL (pass is 8.5). This is a genuinely strong spec: numeric density is exceptional (alpha 0.32–0.46, hue 190–202°, 34–42 px glyphs on 44–52 px centres, WCAG ≥4.5:1, 0 px² intersection on eight named selector pairs), it carries its own anchored ui-specific score table instead of borrowing the photorealism anchors, its dependency signatures and line citations are verified-correct against the code, its failure modes are drawn verbatim from ui_r1.md and ui_r2.json rather than being generic advice, and 17 of 22 acceptance items are mechanically checkable with the probe named. It does not pass because four defects will each cost or partly waste a round rather than merely lean on judgement: item 21's photo-mode hint is unachievable as written (dt is wall-clock-derived at speed=0, so a ≤3 s fade is always over by capture, yet item 11 and §8 require a visible hint in photo_22.png, and the §6 bullet's stated rationale for preferring dt over CSS is wrong); the item 3 six-rail mapping mathematically caps the three green rails at 40/35/25 % fill, which contradicts the §3 cs2_3 target the same section pushes the builder toward, and names no selector for rail-vs-fill so the width-ratio probe has no defined operands; the 8.5 anchor lets item 19 (budget) fail while CRITIC.md makes budget a hard pass gate; and the card/category inventory is unbounded — "every card in every category" with no category list and no total count is an open-ended workload two builders will size very differently. Add the duplication of BUILDER.md's lane rules in §7 (which the spec's own header claims not to restate), the §5-vs-§8 draw-call contradiction, and two factual errors, and this sits at 8.0. All the fixes are small local edits; none require re-measuring the references.
